name: home-ahead
description: Home Ahead: Alexa+ household assistant for devices, recalls and repairs

paragraphs: A home that keeps up with your baby. Home Ahead is an Alexa+ add-on (shown here as a simulated Alexa+ experience) and a self-hosted MCP server. It checks hand-me-downs against real U.S. recall notices, re-checks the home every time a child learns a new move, orders the safety supplies after you confirm, and tells you when a new recall reaches something you own.

Built for the Build, Ship, Shape: Amazon Developer Hackathon, Alexa+ track. Home Ahead is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon. The Alexa+ screen in this repo is a simulation.

Babyproofing is usually done once, before the baby arrives. But the risks in a home change with every new move: a dresser that was fine for a crawler can tip onto a baby who pulls up on it, and blind cords come within reach. Families also lean on hand-me-downs (high chairs, cribs, dressers), and recalled products keep circulating long after a recall is announced.
features: Checks hand-me-downs on the spot. "My sister is giving us her old high chair." It asks for the model number on the label, matches it against U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) recall notices, and says…

Re-checks the home when the baby changes. "She pulled herself up on the couch today!" The child moves to the pulling up and cruising stage, the room-by-room plan updates (anchor the dresser, strap the TV, get blind…

Watches for new recalls. When a recall that matches something in the home is published, the screen shows an alert without being asked. Because the family already anchored that dresser, it can say the dresser can stay in…
